title: Design a Fix That Can Be Tested

scenes.tts: The first film followed nutrients from land to low oxygen. Where should a limited cleanup budget act? A useful plan cuts the cause first, rebuilds habitat, and works within real limits.
scenes.caption: The first film followed nutrients from land to low oxygen. Where should a limited cleanup budget act? A useful plan cuts the cause first, rebuilds habitat, and works within real limits.
scenes.visual: Rebuild the first film's labelled schematic watershed exactly: field at left, river through the middle, Bay at right. Use the same orange nutrients, green algae, blue oxygen, cyan surface water, navy bottom water, and gold habitat. Add a large budget bar above it.
scenes.narration: The first film followed nutrients from land to low oxygen. Where should a limited cleanup budget act? A useful plan cuts the cause first, rebuilds habitat, and works within real limits.

scenes.visual: Keep the moving watershed dimly visible. Show the title Design a Fix That Can Be Tested for two seconds, then restore the map.

scenes.tts: Restoration means returning a damaged ecosystem toward health. Criteria say what a solution must achieve, such as lowering nitrogen or adding habitat. Constraints are limits, including money, land, and time. The budget bar is one constraint, so every choice has a trade-off.
scenes.caption: Restoration means returning a damaged ecosystem toward health. Criteria say what a solution must achieve, such as lowering nitrogen or adding habitat. Constraints are limits, including money, land, and time. The budget bar is one constraint, so every choice has a trade-off.
scenes.visual: Place two large cards over the map: criteria and constraints. Under criteria, animate an orange nutrient arrow shrinking and gold habitat expanding. Under constraints, divide the budget bar into money, land, and time segments. Keep all labels large.
scenes.narration: Restoration means returning a damaged ecosystem toward health. Criteria say what a solution must achieve, such as lowering nitrogen or adding habitat. Constraints are limits, including money, land, and time. The budget bar is one constraint, so every choice has a trade-off.

scenes.tts: Start upstream. A forest buffer is a strip of trees and shrubs beside a stream. It slows runoff, traps soil, and can remove nitrate from water underground. Winter cover crops hold soil and take up leftover nitrogen. Both act before nutrients reach the Bay.
scenes.caption: Start upstream. A forest buffer is a strip of trees and shrubs beside a stream. It slows runoff, traps soil, and can remove nitrate from water underground. Winter cover crops hold soil and take up leftover nitrogen. Both act before nutrients reach the Bay.
scenes.visual: Grow a wide green buffer along the carried stream and a low cover crop across the field. Animate some orange markers stopping in roots and soil while others continue. Add the label effect varies with place beside the buffer, without a numerical claim.
scenes.narration: Start upstream. A forest buffer is a strip of trees and shrubs beside a stream. It slows runoff, traps soil, and can remove nitrate from water underground. Winter cover crops hold soil and take up leftover nitrogen. Both act before nutrients reach the Bay.

scenes.tts: Wastewater upgrades remove more nitrogen at a treatment plant. Oyster reefs work differently. Oysters filter particles, and the reef shelters other animals. Reefs rebuild habitat, but they do not replace cutting nutrients. In this plan, underwater grass is a readout, not a tool. Cleaner water can let it return where conditions suit it.
scenes.caption: Wastewater upgrades remove more nitrogen at a treatment plant. Oyster reefs work differently. Oysters filter particles, and the reef shelters other animals. Reefs rebuild habitat, but they do not replace cutting nutrients. In this plan, underwater grass is a readout, not a tool. Cleaner water can let it return where conditions suit it.
scenes.visual: At the plant, divert orange markers into a treatment loop and return clearer flow. In the Bay, grow a gold oyster reef with small animals sheltering there. A pale grass bed brightens only after the water above it clears. Keep a separate orange stream visible to show that habitat alone does not remove the upstream source.
scenes.narration: Wastewater upgrades remove more nitrogen at a treatment plant. Oyster reefs work differently. Oysters filter particles, and the reef shelters other animals. Reefs rebuild habitat, but they do not replace cutting nutrients. In this plan, underwater grass is a readout, not a tool. Cleaner water can let it return where conditions suit it.

scenes.tts: Place each tool beside the step it can change. Land and treatment tools can reduce orange nutrient flow. Reefs add habitat directly, and cleaner water can let underwater grass return. So a plan cuts nutrients first, then adds habitat as its criteria and budget allow.
scenes.caption: Place each tool beside the step it can change. Land and treatment tools can reduce orange nutrient flow. Reefs add habitat directly, and cleaner water can let underwater grass return. So a plan cuts nutrients first, then adds habitat as its criteria and budget allow.
scenes.visual: Draw two large paths across the carried map. The pressure path links buffer, cover crop, and wastewater plant to a shrinking orange arrow. The habitat path links the reef to an expanding gold patch, and a dotted arrow runs from the shrinking orange arrow to a returning grass bed. Keep the budget bar visible above both.

scenes.tts: No single readout tells the whole story. Nitrogen load, the total delivered over time, tracks a pressure entering the Bay. Summer oxygen tracks a condition animals need. Underwater grass tracks habitat. A plan may improve one before another, so keep all three gauges beside the same map.
scenes.caption: No single readout tells the whole story. Nitrogen load, the total delivered over time, tracks a pressure entering the Bay. Summer oxygen tracks a condition animals need. Underwater grass tracks habitat. A plan may improve one before another, so keep all three gauges beside the same map.
scenes.visual: Transform the criteria cards into three large schematic gauges labelled nitrogen load, summer oxygen, and underwater grass. Link each gauge to its location on the watershed. Move one gauge at a time to demonstrate that the readouts need not change together.
scenes.narration: No single readout tells the whole story. Nitrogen load, the total delivered over time, tracks a pressure entering the Bay. Summer oxygen tracks a condition animals need. Underwater grass tracks habitat. A plan may improve one before another, so keep all three gauges beside the same map.

scenes.tts: Suppose nutrient flow drops after a new fix. Which change should appear first: less nutrient pressure, or a fully regrown grass bed?
scenes.caption: Suppose nutrient flow drops after a new fix. Which change should appear first: less nutrient pressure, or a fully regrown grass bed?
scenes.visual: Show two equally sized outcome cards above the map: a smaller orange nutrient arrow and a full gold grass bed. Put Which appears first? between them. Do not highlight either choice.
scenes.narration: Suppose nutrient flow drops after a new fix. Which change should appear first: less nutrient pressure, or a fully regrown grass bed?

scenes.visual: Hold both outcome cards for thinking. Keep stream flow and grass sway moving slowly. Do not reveal the answer.

scenes.tts: Less nutrient pressure can appear first. Grass recovery often lags: the water must clear, and plants need time to spread back. Stored nitrogen can also keep leaking from soil for years, so even the nutrient drop can be slow. Track each criterion over time instead of judging one sample.
scenes.caption: Less nutrient pressure can appear first. Grass recovery often lags: the water must clear, and plants need time to spread back. Stored nitrogen can also keep leaking from soil for years, so even the nutrient drop can be slow. Track each criterion over time instead of judging one sample.
scenes.visual: Move the smaller orange arrow forward on a schematic timeline before the gold grass bed expands. Add a slowly draining soil store upstream and water above the grass clearing before the bed spreads. Label the timeline schematic.
scenes.narration: Less nutrient pressure can appear first. Grass recovery often lags: the water must clear, and plants need time to spread back. Stored nitrogen can also keep leaking from soil for years, so even the nutrient drop can be slow. Track each criterion over time instead of judging one sample.

scenes.tts: A strong plan states what evidence would count before work begins. Measure the pressure, the condition, and the habitat response. Repeat measurements across several years. Keep the comparison fair, and report when the evidence supports only part of the plan.
scenes.caption: A strong plan states what evidence would count before work begins. Measure the pressure, the condition, and the habitat response. Repeat measurements across several years. Keep the comparison fair, and report when the evidence supports only part of the plan.
scenes.visual: Place a large clipboard beside the three gauges. Check off pressure, condition, habitat, repeated measurements, and fair comparison as the corresponding objects pulse on the map. Leave the final result box partly filled rather than showing certain success.
scenes.narration: A strong plan states what evidence would count before work begins. Measure the pressure, the condition, and the habitat response. Repeat measurements across several years. Keep the comparison fair, and report when the evidence supports only part of the plan.

scenes.tts: Build the plan, measure the results, and compare them with a place that received no fix. If results are unclear, refine the design and test again. The causal chain tells you where to act. Measured criteria tell you whether the plan works.
scenes.caption: Build the plan, measure the results, and compare them with a place that received no fix. If results are unclear, refine the design and test again. The causal chain tells you where to act. Measured criteria tell you whether the plan works.
scenes.visual: Split the carried watershed into matched fix and comparison panels. Animate a loop around both: build, measure, compare, refine. Return to one map with smaller orange flow, a higher blue gauge, and more gold habitat, each shown as a possible goal rather than a guaranteed result.
scenes.narration: Build the plan, measure the results, and compare them with a place that received no fix. If results are unclear, refine the design and test again. The causal chain tells you where to act. Measured criteria tell you whether the plan works.

scenes.visual: Clear everything to one centered line only: 'Effective fixes cut nutrients first, rebuild habitat, and track recovery over time.'
